events.description: Grant of land from Emperor Henry VI; Monaco refounded in 1215 as a colony of Genoa.
Monaco refounded as a colony of Genoa following the imperial land grant.
Francesco Grimaldi and his men captured the fortress of the Rock of Monaco, dressed as Franciscan friars, establishing Grimaldi rule.
Revolutionary French forces captured Monaco; the principality was occupied until 1814.
Monaco designated a protectorate of the Kingdom of Sardinia by the Congress of Vienna.
Italian Army invaded and occupied Monaco in 1943, forming a fascist administration. In September 1943, German Wehrmacht occupied Monaco after Mussolini's fall.
Nazi deportation of the Jewish population of Monaco began in September 1943 following German occupation.

entries.notes: Hecataeus refers to Monaco as a Ligurian town; Ligurians were a pre-Roman Italic/Celtic people of the region. No specific archaeological culture named for this site; using Gauls as closest attested regional culture. Closed at Roman period.
Roman presence in the western Mediterranean from the 2nd century BC; Monaco area under Roman influence. Closed at the fall of the Western Roman Empire.
Ligurian/Gaulish dialects spoken in the region before Roman conquest. Closed with Latin dominance from the 1st century BC.
Latin spread with Roman conquest; ceased as spoken vernacular and was replaced by Italian/Old French dialects in the early medieval period.
Italian was the official language until replaced by French in 1860. Approximate start date from the medieval period.
entries.sources: Italian was the official language in Monaco until 1860
Italian was the official language in Monaco until 1860, when it was replaced by French

entries.notes: Strabo mentions a temple of Heracles (Monoikos) at Monaco, attesting Greek religious presence. Closed circa 4th–5th century AD with Christianisation.
Roman religious practice from the Roman period. Closed with Christianisation circa 4th–5th century AD.
Christianity became dominant in the region from the 4th–5th century AD. Catholicism has been the state religion of Monaco to the present day.
Mentioned by Hecataeus of Miletus as a Ligurian town; approximate date for ancient attestation.
